claim: The new docs paragraph names the feature toggle as `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`, but the registered and evaluated name is `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`, and no prefix normalization exists, so an operator following the docs silently gets no effect.
raw: **Issue:** The new docs paragraph says the setting "Requires the `dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` [feature toggle] to be enabled." The registered and evaluated name is `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` (`pkg/services/featuremgmt/registry.go:2253`; `pkg/setting/setting.go:763`).

claim: The `/api/gnet/*` route proxies any HTTP method and any caller-controlled path to Grafana.com with the instance credential, reachable by any signed-in user and even anonymously when anonymous access is enabled.
raw: **Issue:** `r.Any("/api/gnet/*", requestmeta.SetSLOGroup(...), reqSignedIn, hs.ProxyGnetRequest)`. `r.Any` registers `Handle("*", ...)` — all HTTP methods. `ProxyGnetRequest` takes `web.Params(c.Req)["*"]` verbatim, and the director deletes the caller's `Authorization` header and substitutes `Bearer <instance grafana.com token>`.

claim: The CLI accessor prefers `proxy_token` with no feature-flag check (and grafana-cli cannot evaluate the flag at all), so the toggle is not a kill switch and server and CLI can use different tokens against the same API.
raw: The server path (`pkg/setting/setting.go:763`) gates the same decision on `grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken`. `grafana-cli` never calls `featuremgmt.InitOpenFeatureWithCfg` — the only callers are `pkg/cmd/grafana-server/commands/{cli,target}.go` and `pkg/tests/testinfra/testinfra.go` — so the CLI cannot evaluate the flag even in principle.

claim: `ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` is an unenforced post-load lifecycle contract, so a bootstrap that skips it (e.g. `pkg/tests/testinfra/testinfra.go:124`) yields an empty token and an unauthenticated outbound request with no error or log.
raw: The change repoints them at `cfg.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken` (`pkg/api/grafana_com_proxy.go:54`, `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginconfig/config.go:39`), whose *effective* value is produced only by a post-load mutator called from exactly two places (`cli.go:113`, `target.go:99`). The contract exists solely as a doc comment; nothing enforces or detects it.

claim: `applyCommandLineProperties` appends `cfg:` command-line overrides unredacted to `appliedCommandLineProperties`, which `LogConfigSources` writes at Info level, so a secret passed via `cfg:` is logged in plaintext despite the new `PROXY_TOKEN$` redaction pattern.
raw: This change adds `"PROXY_TOKEN$"` to the `RedactedValue` pattern list (`setting.go:828-831`), correctly covering the env-var and INI paths. But `applyCommandLineProperties` (`setting.go:1145-1160`) appends the **raw** value ... while its sibling `applyCommandLineDefaultProperties` (`setting.go:1139`) formats through `RedactedValue(keyString, value)`.

claim: The new feature-toggle registry entry omits `RequiresRestart: true` even though the flag is read once at startup, so the toggles API tells operators no restart is needed when one is.
raw: **Issue:** The flag's only consumer resolves it exactly once during `RunServer`/`RunTargetServer` and bakes the result into `cfg.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken`; nothing re-evaluates it. `toggles_gen.csv:265` confirms the generated metadata reports `RequiresRestart` as `false`. 40 sibling entries in the same file set `RequiresRestart: true` for exactly this class of startup-only effect.

claim: The flag name is a hardcoded string literal instead of the generated `featuremgmt` constant, and the test hardcodes the same literal, so a rename silently disables the feature with no compile-time or test guard.
raw: **Issue:** The evaluation hardcodes `"grafana.dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken"` rather than `featuremgmt.FlagGrafanaDedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken` (`toggles_gen.go:727`). Every other flag consumer in the repo uses the generated constant ... The generated constant currently has **zero references anywhere in the tree**.

claim: The OpenFeature `Boolean` call discards the evaluation error and resolution reason and nothing logs which token source was selected, so a provider failure is indistinguishable from the flag being off.
raw: **Issue:** `openfeature.NewDefaultClient().Boolean(...)` discards both the error and the resolution reason, inside a method that returns nothing — so there is no channel at all through which a failed evaluation can surface. Three distinct paths land on the same silent outcome: flag off (the shipped default), flag on but `proxy_token` empty, and provider error. None is logged.

claim: The new subtest "uses dedicated token when flag is on and proxy_token is set" is tautological — it still passes with the resolver gutted to a no-op, because `cfg.Load()` already set the asserted field.
raw: The subtest *"uses dedicated token when flag is on and proxy_token is set"* asserts `cfg.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken == "dedicated-token"` after calling the resolver. But `cfg.Load()` has **already** set that field to `dedicated-token` from `GF_GRAFANA_COM_PROXY_TOKEN` before the resolver runs. ... The subtest passes with the entire function gutted.

claim: The only CLI token test still asserts `GcomToken()`, which production no longer calls, leaving the new `GrafanaComProxyAPIToken()` preference logic untested in both branches.
raw: **Issue:** `newInstallPluginOpts` (`install_command.go:102`) was changed to call `c.GrafanaComProxyAPIToken()`. `TestIntegrationPluginRepoConfig` still asserts `c.GcomToken() == "token3"` — a method with zero remaining production callers. The new accessor's preference logic (`proxy_token` wins; else fall back to `sso_api_token`) has **no** coverage in either branch.

claim: The plugin repo client attaches the Grafana.com token using an unanchored string prefix match on the configured base URL, so the credential can be sent to a non-Grafana.com or lookalike host.
raw: `c.grafanaComAPIURL` comes from the manager's `BaseURL`, which for the CLI is `--repo` / `GF_PLUGIN_REPO` / `api_url`. Two consequences: the token is sent to any configured non-Grafana.com repo host with no check that it *is* Grafana.com; and if the configured base URL has no path component (e.g. `api_url = https://gcom.internal`), the prefix test is not anchored at a host boundary.

claim: `GcomToken()` has zero remaining production call sites but is retained on the exported `CommandLine` interface, its implementation, and the mock, leaving two near-identical token accessors side by side.
raw: **Issue:** Verified by grep: after `install_command.go:102` switched, `GcomToken()`'s only remaining references are the interface declaration, its implementation, the mock, and test doubles — **zero** production call sites.

claim: `proxy_token` was added to `conf/defaults.ini` but not mirrored into the annotated `conf/sample.ini` `[grafana_com]` section, so operators reading the sample never learn the option exists.
raw: **Issue:** `[grafana_com]` in `sample.ini` mirrors `defaults.ini` — `;url`, `;api_url`, and `;sso_api_token` with an explanatory comment. `proxy_token` was added to `defaults.ini:1899` but not mirrored, so operators editing the annotated sample never learn the option exists.

claim: The new docs entry uses a Hugo `relref` shortcode — the only one in the file — where the documented convention and every sibling link use plain inline Markdown links.
raw: **Issue:** `docs/AGENTS.md:110` states: "Use inline Markdown links: `[Link text](https://example.com)`." The new `[feature toggle]({{< relref "#feature_toggles" >}})` is the **only** `relref` in this ~3000-line file (verified: `grep -c relref` returns 1).

claim: `proxy_token` is added bare with no comment saying it is inert without the feature toggle and falls back to `sso_api_token`, unlike its documented sibling `sso_api_token`.
raw: `conf/defaults.ini:1899` — `proxy_token` added bare, with no comment saying it is inert without the feature toggle and falls back to `sso_api_token`; `sample.ini`'s `sso_api_token` carries one (knowledge-reviewer, broad-reviewer)

claim: The per-setting "Set via environment variable: GF_GRAFANA_COM_PROXY_TOKEN" callout is the only one of its kind in the file, duplicating the generic override rule stated once up front.
raw: `docs/.../_index.md:2327` — "Set via environment variable: `GF_GRAFANA_COM_PROXY_TOKEN`." is the only such per-setting callout for a standard `GF_`-prefixed key in the file; the doc states the generic override rule once, up front at lines 79-82 (consistency-reviewer)

claim: `Test_readGrafanaComSettings_GrafanaComProxyAPIToken` tests a `[grafana_com]` key but is placed among plugin-settings tests rather than with the other `parseINIFile` tests.
raw: `pkg/setting/setting_plugins_test.go:284` — `Test_readGrafanaComSettings_GrafanaComProxyAPIToken` tests a `[grafana_com]` key but lives among plugin-settings tests rather than with the other `parseINIFile` tests in `setting_test.go` (test-reviewer)

claim: No test asserts which token reaches the `Authorization` header under either flag state; the file has no test file at all.
raw: `pkg/api/grafana_com_proxy.go:54` — no test asserts which token reaches the `Authorization` header under either flag state; no test file exists for this file at all (test-reviewer, broad-reviewer, security-reviewer)

claim: `ProvidePluginManagementConfig`'s propagation of the new token is untested.
raw: `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginconfig/config.go:39` — `ProvidePluginManagementConfig`'s token propagation is untested (test-reviewer, broad-reviewer)

claim: No test pins the idempotency / second-call contract of the resolver.
raw: `pkg/setting/setting.go:762` — no test pins the idempotency / second-call contract of the resolver (design-reviewer)

claim: `setProvider`'s cleanup restores `openfeature.NoopProvider{}` rather than the previously installed provider, permanently replacing process-global SDK state for the rest of the test binary (no failure today).
raw: `pkg/setting/setting_test.go:400` — `setProvider`'s cleanup restores `openfeature.NoopProvider{}` rather than the provider installed before the subtest, permanently replacing process-global SDK state for the rest of the package's test binary. No failure today (nothing else in `pkg/setting` evaluates flags), and go-reviewer verified there is no data race

claim: No audit log records who drove a proxied grafana.com call with the instance credential, so misuse of the gnet proxy is unattributable after the fact.
raw: `pkg/api/grafana_com_proxy.go:52` — no audit log records who drove a proxied grafana.com call with the instance credential, so misuse via #2 is unattributable after the fact (security-reviewer)

claim: Grafana Enterprise entry points outside this repository would need the same `ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken()` insertion, and nothing in the change makes that requirement discoverable from the OSS side.
raw: Grafana Enterprise entry points are outside this repository. If Enterprise has its own `RunServer` equivalent, it needs the same `ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken()` insertion, and nothing in this change makes that requirement discoverable from the OSS side (broad, adversarial, go)

claim: Four reviewers claimed the resolver destroys the configured `proxy_token`, making resolution one-way and non-idempotent — refuted by the validation wave since `cfg.Raw` retains the original value and the resolver has two mutually exclusive single-call sites.
raw: **"The resolver destroys the configured `proxy_token`, making resolution one-way"** (knowledge, design, adversarial, go — 4 finders, Medium/High) — **refuted**. The overwrite at `setting.go:766` is real, but every claimed consequence fails ... What remains is a style preference with no reachable failure.

claim: Claimed that passing an empty `openfeature.EvaluationContext{}` instead of `TransactionContext(ctx)` erases global context — refuted from the SDK source.
raw: **Empty `openfeature.EvaluationContext{}` instead of `TransactionContext(ctx)`** — refuted by two reviewers from the SDK source: `mergeContexts` only adopts lower-precedence attributes when higher-precedence ones are absent, so an empty invocation context cannot erase the global context `InitOpenFeatureWithCfg` installs.

claim: Claimed that `context.Background()` with no timeout on a possibly-remote flag evaluation can hang — dismissed because the transport layer already sets timeouts.
raw: **`context.Background()` with no timeout on a possibly-remote flag evaluation** — bounded at the transport layer; `pkg/infra/features/client.go:47-66` sets both `Timeout` and `DialTimeout`.

claim: Claimed `logger.Debug("Could not parse config file", err)` is a structured-logger arity bug — refuted, the CLI logger is a `fmt.Println` wrapper with no key/value contract.
raw: **`logger.Debug("Could not parse config file", err)` as a structured-logger arity bug** — refuted. `pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/logger` is not `pkg/infra/log`; its `Debug(args ...any)` is a `fmt.Println` wrapper. No key/value contract exists.

claim: Claimed `skipStaticRootValidation = true` is set without restore in the new test — refuted as redundant, since the package global is already set unconditionally elsewhere.
raw: **`skipStaticRootValidation = true` set without restore at `setting_test.go:388`** — refuted by two reviewers: the package global is already set unconditionally at `setting_test.go:30` and `setting_session_test.go:13`, and it only guards a function that emits a log line and always returns nil. Redundant, not newly harmful.

claim: Claimed the new mock's `ret.Get(0).(string)` panics on nil — dismissed as identical to every sibling method and standard mockery contract.
raw: **`ret.Get(0).(string)` panicking on nil in the new mock** — identical to every sibling method in the file; standard mockery contract.

claim: Claimed a runtime `Cfg` reload would invalidate the one-time resolution — dismissed, no runtime reload path exists in OSS.
raw: **Runtime `Cfg` reload invalidating the resolution** — searched `pkg/setting`, `pkg/services/settingsprovider`, `pkg/api`; no runtime reload path exists in OSS.

claim: Claimed the token could leak via redirect from the plugin repo client — dismissed, Go's http.Client strips `Authorization` on cross-host redirects.
raw: **Token leakage via redirect from the plugin repo client** — Go's `http.Client` strips `Authorization` on cross-host redirects.

claim: Claimed the `PROXY_TOKEN$` redaction pattern is too broad — dismissed, over-redaction is the safe direction and no key currently collides.
raw: **`PROXY_TOKEN$` redaction pattern breadth** — will redact any key ending in `PROXY_TOKEN`; over-redaction is the safe direction, and no other key in `conf/` or `pkg/` currently collides.

claim: Claimed the resolved token could be exposed via `/api/admin/settings` — dismissed, `AdminGetSettings` serializes the redacting SettingsProvider, not the `Cfg` struct.
raw: **Config exposure via `/api/admin/settings`** — `AdminGetSettings` serializes `SettingsProvider.Current()`, which redacts through `RedactedValue(EnvKey(...))`; it does not serialize the `Cfg` struct, so the resolved field is unreachable.

claim: Claimed the registry entry's `Generate{Go: true}` deviates from siblings' `Generate{LegacyGo: true, LegacyFrontend: true}` — dismissed as an established alternate pattern.
raw: **`Generate{Go: true}` vs siblings' `Generate{LegacyGo: true, LegacyFrontend: true}`** — an established alternate pattern used 9 other times in `registry.go`.

claim: Claimed the `toggles_gen.json` tombstone churn (four historical flag names) is a defect — dismissed as generated output of the rename history.
raw: **`toggles_gen.json` tombstone churn** (four historical names) — generated-file output of the rename history. Not a defect, but cited as evidence in #1 and #7.

claim: Claimed `%2e%2e` in the gnet wildcard may escape the `/api` prefix — left unresolved (not cleared) because settling it requires a running instance.
raw: **Path traversal through the gnet proxy** (`%2e%2e` escaping the `/api` prefix) — adversarial-reviewer could not confirm whether the router normalizes the wildcard remainder before `web.Params`; two unconfirmed steps, anchor 25. Requires a running instance to settle. **Unresolved, not cleared.**

claim: Claimed `c.Config()` re-parses the whole INI file on every CLI accessor call — dismissed as a pre-existing pattern with cost only in a one-shot CLI process.
raw: **`c.Config()` re-parsing the whole INI file on every CLI accessor call** — pre-existing pattern shared with `GcomToken`/`PluginRepoURL`; cost only, one-shot CLI process.

claim: Claimed a whitespace-only `proxy_token` is accepted and sent as `Bearer  ` unlike the sibling token which trims — dismissed as contained, outcome is a plain 401.
raw: **Whitespace-only `proxy_token`** accepted (`" "` is non-empty → `Bearer  ` sent); `pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:57` does `TrimSpace` on the sibling token. Contained — outcome is a plain 401.

claim: Claimed the legacy `[grafana_net]` alias does not apply to `proxy_token` — dismissed, the alias only ever applied to `url` and `sso_api_token` behaves identically.
raw: **`[grafana_net]` legacy alias not applying to `proxy_token`** — verified it only ever applied to `url` (`setting.go:1669-1671`); `sso_api_token` behaves identically. Not a regression.

claim: Threat-model note: the change is net-neutral by default — it builds the mechanism for credential separation without engaging it, and does not narrow what `/api/gnet/*` proxies, who can reach it, or what it does with the token.
raw: **Attack-surface change.** Net-neutral by default; net-positive only when the toggle is on **and** `proxy_token` is populated. The change does not narrow what `/api/gnet/*` will proxy, who can reach it, or what it will do with the token. **Summary the reviewer offered, which the evidence supports:** this change builds the mechanism for credential separation without engaging it.
